specialScreening.text: El Al: check-in T4 floor 2 (desks 986–989), connecting passengers to T4S floor 1, boarding area S (Aena); feed TLV departures of LY use S31 / S34. El Al security questioning is reported by travellers (anecdotal); its time is not published.

deadline.text: Iberia, flights to Israel: be at the boarding gate at least 90 min before departure (additional mandatory controls at the gate; Iberia time-limit page, owner capture 2026-11-02). A gate-arrival deadline, not the duration of the check

specialScreening.text: Iberia flights to Tel Aviv (Madrid T4 Satellite): Iberia states additional mandatory security controls at the boarding gate and asks passengers to be at the gate at least 90 min before departure; check-in closes 55 min before departure (T4S). How long the gate control takes is not published. Applies to Iberia-marketed and operated flights per the Iberia page; other airlines are not covered by it.

Flights to Israel: whether this airline has an additional document check, interview or separate screening at Madrid-Barajas (only El Al and Iberia are documented) is not established by any source we could read. Allow extra time and check with the airline.

US-bound flights: TSA / DHS enhanced security measures for all last-point-of-departure airports (2017, still the baseline as far as known) may add checks at check-in or at the gate (interviews, document checks, separate screening of electronics). The procedures are not public; no time is known.

rules.text: Border zones: T1 gates A and B are non-Schengen; gates C and D (T1–T2) and E (T3) are Schengen/domestic; T4 gates H, J and K are Schengen/domestic; T4 Satellite has the non-Schengen S gates (with R and U letters at the ends) on floor 1 and a few Schengen M gates on floor 0 (exceptional Iberia / Iberia Express / Air Nostrum Schengen flights).

Two separate hubs: T1–T2–T3 (walkable, landside and airside) and T4–T4S (linked only by the APM), about 4 km apart. Between them, passengers go landside on the free 24-h shuttle bus and pass security again — except non-Schengen ↔ non-Schengen connections with a boarding card and bags checked through, which use the on-request airside bus between T1 baggage hall 1 and T4S floor 0.

T4S passport control: departing passengers to S gates pass it on floor −1 after the APM; arriving S passengers pass it on floor 2 before the APM to T4 (baggage hall 10). Non-Schengen ↔ non-Schengen transfers in T4S use the international connections security without passport control.

No minimum connection time is published on the Aena pages read (they refer to airline information and, for PRM passengers, the Barrier Free service). Iberia (search excerpt of its connection-times page, not fetched: 403) gives 45 min within one building and 55 min between T4 and T4S for Iberia/Air Nostrum connections, 75–90 min when other airlines are involved. Guides quote 45–60 min for a T1/T2 ↔ T4 transfer with re-screening (Points Analyst, 2026). Not used for routing.

Expansion programme (DORA 2027–2031, > €4 bn): T4 central security filter fully reopened late July 2026; tenders approved July 2026 for the T4S south pier (+36 m, 3 contact positions, 24 months) and the T4 north apron (remote stands, 35 months); later a new processor and renewed boarding areas in T1–T3. No passenger-area closure dated for autumn 2026 was found. Metro L5 extension to T1-T2-T3 is under construction (OSM).

Baggage (Aena connecting page, re-read 2026-11-01): Aena gives separate instructions for passengers who do NOT have to collect baggage or check in (bags checked through) and those who do. With bags checked through, only T1 A/B ↔ T4S S (non-Schengen ↔ non-Schengen) stays airside, on the transfer bus called by the Green Jackets desk; every other T1/T2/T3 ↔ T4/T4S connection leaves the transit zone ("access Spanish territory") and re-enters through security. With bags to collect (separate tickets, bags not through), the passenger reclaims them (Ryanair and easyJet arrivals in hall 5), checks in again (Ryanair and easyJet departures at T1 level 1, others at T2 level 2, T1 level 1 or T4 level 2) and passes security and passport control again, even for S → S in T4S (APM to hall 10 and back). EU law: hold baggage from a non-EU airport transferred onto an intra-EU flight is customs-controlled at the last international EU airport of arrival, unless the Member State applies the control at MAD for an onward flight to another Spanish international airport (not settled by any source read); cabin baggage at MAD. The model has no reclaim or check-in step: self-transfer times exclude the belt wait and bag drop.

openQuestions.question: Which M gate numbers exist in T4S today (M22–M51 per an Iberia document), and which stands they share with the S/R/U gates?
openQuestions.impact: Only M22, M28 and M51 are listed; a flight at another M gate maps to the M area only by its letter.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Owner capture of Iberia’s "More on T4" page (iberia.com is 403 to automated fetches) or a dated photo of the T4S floor-0 gate signs.

openQuestions.question: Are the south-end T4S gates signed R (OSM, Wikipedia, guides) or S (Aena lists Iberia desks at "gates S15–S16")? Are the U gates still signed U?
openQuestions.impact: Gate lookup for R1–R18 / S15–S16 / U55–U74; zone is non-Schengen either way.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Photo of the T4S floor-1 directory or the Aena interactive map (owner capture).

openQuestions.question: Does the APM keep arriving and departing passengers on separate platforms/cars, and can a departing passenger in T4S (M zone) ride back to T4 H/J/K?
openQuestions.impact: Routes M → H/J/K use the departures side in reverse (inferred); arrivals are routed through baggage hall 10 and connection security.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Walkthrough video of the T4 −2 level showing both platforms, or Aena confirmation.

openQuestions.question: Do S-arrival passengers connecting to H/J/K always pass the connection security at baggage hall 10 (Aena text), or can they go up directly from the APM ("Gates / Puertas H J K" sign)? A 2024 walking tour (Matt Drones, t≈540–560 s) goes from the T4 APM platform up the escalators straight into the T4 duty-free and J gates within ~20 s of footage; the APM ride is cut, so a security checkpoint may have been edited out.
openQuestions.impact: One transfer-security allowance on S → H/J/K routes.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Dated video of the T4 APM arrival platform following the "Gates H J K" signs.

openQuestions.question: Exact layout of the T1 checkpoint: does T1 security open into the Schengen C zone (inferred) and where precisely is the passport control "to the right"? Are there B gates B1–B17 and A15+?
openQuestions.impact: T1 landside → C/D route is inferred; gate coverage of T1 is partial.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Aena terminal map (owner capture) or a 2025–2026 T1 departures walkthrough with readable signs.

openQuestions.question: Typical wait of the on-request transfer bus T1 hall 1 ↔ T4S (no frequency published; "upon request" at Aena, "frequency upon demand" at Iberia), and its door-to-door ride (≈ 12 min observed, 2022). Aena: the Green Jackets information desk in the T1 baggage hall calls the internal shuttle (re-read 2026-11-01). Iberia search excerpts (pages not fetched, 403) say passengers can use the interphones if a shuttle wait exceeds 10 minutes, but it is unclear which shuttle (T4 connection centre or T1/T2/T3 arrivals stops) the sentence refers to, so the assumed wait is not changed.
openQuestions.impact: Wait (15 min) is assumed; ride (10 min) from a 2022 video.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Recent first-hand report or Aena/Iberia transfer guidance.

openQuestions.question: Which T1–T4S gates are bus (remote) gates? OSM range nodes (B18–B20, B21–B25, B26–B29) and a 2025 video (stairs to an apron bus in T1) suggest bus boarding, but no gate number is attested.
openQuestions.impact: No gate is marked bus: true.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Gate-level photos or the Aena map.

openQuestions.question: Are the T1, T2 and T4 security checkpoints (and the T1 connections security) open all night? Aena publishes 24-h bus and APM service but no checkpoint hours. Update 2026-11-01: a commercial guide (Valet Barajas, Apr 2026) says the T4 checkpoints are open 24 h with reduced capacity 01:00–04:00; nothing found for T1, T2 or the T1 connections security; the Aena security page lists police and weapons-office hours only.
openQuestions.impact: Night (00:00–05:00) routes landside → airside and T1/T2 ↔ T4 transfers assume the checkpoints are open; if a checkpoint closes, those cells become unroutable at night.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Aena terminal information or an owner/field check at night; add Walk.hours to the security walks.

openQuestions.question: Non-Schengen arrival at MAD connecting on one ticket to a Spanish domestic flight (including the Canary Islands, outside the EU VAT area): are checked bags customs-controlled at MAD (EU 2015/2447 Art. 39(2) option for the same Member State) or at the destination?
openQuestions.impact: If the control is at MAD, those passengers reclaim bags at MAD and the airside or "no bags" route modelled today is wrong for them.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Iberia connection pages (iberia.com / help.iberia.com HTTP 403: owner capture) or Agencia Tributaria / Aena guidance.

openQuestions.question: How long do baggage reclaim and re-check-in take for a self-transfer at MAD (T1 halls 1/2/5, T4 hall 10)?
openQuestions.impact: Self-transfer routes leave through the arrivals exit and re-enter through security, but the belt wait and bag drop are not modelled (no schema field), so these routes are too short.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Schema: a reclaim/bag-drop step or profile flag; data: Aena or uncut video timing.
